* [GK Elite 2026-27 fabric catalogue](gk-elite-fabric-catalogue.md) - GK Elite's 2026-27 fabric lines with compositions, colour codes and counts (39 mystique, 13 hologram, 18 SoftLux, 72-colour sublimation palette), plus the swatch store's wider lists, design routes and production times.
* [Fabric mills and wholesalers](mills-and-wholesalers.md) - Who supplies leotard fabric and what they publish: Carvico (the only mill with full technical sheets), Pine Crest, Spandex World, Solid Stone, Funki, DSI London, Blue Moon, Eurojersey; terms, origins and which makers' suppliers are unknown.

# Design Rule

* [Rule family: colour bleed between adjacent panels](rule-colour-bleed.md) - Dark or bright fabrics (GK flags Navy, Berry, Merlot, Black, Red mystique and Rich Red velvet) next to white or light panels risk colour transfer; warn when a flagged colour touches a light one.
* [Rule family: decoration and trim compatibility by fabric](rule-decoration-and-trim-compatibility.md) - Some fabrics cannot take heat-applied Spanglez or imprinting (velvet, mesh, mesh foil, novelty mesh, rib), only some can be binding or piping, and heat-set stones dull foil; per-fabric compatibility flags.
* [Rule family: mesh lining and accent-only use](rule-mesh-lining-and-accent-use.md) - Mesh on the bodice needs a lining layer, mesh should be an accent rather than the main body, and mesh designs carry a fragility waiver at GK; checks with adjustable defaults.
* [Rule family: stretch matching and fit-changing combinations](rule-stretch-matching.md) - Fabrics joined in one garment should have similar stretch, and heavy embellishment, metallic, lined and mesh areas change fit; warn when panel stretch differs beyond a default threshold or a fit-changing combination is used.
* [Rule family: sublimation artwork and ink palettes](rule-sublimation-ink-on-coloured-base.md) - Sublimation artwork is allowed only on polyester print bases; on a coloured base each base colour permits a short list of darker inks (GK grey takes black only); white in artwork means unprinted cloth.

# Domain Concept

* [Base cloth plus surface finish](base-cloth-and-finish-model.md) - Every catalogued leotard fabric is one of about eight base constructions carrying one of about seven surface finishes, with base colour and finish colour as independent settings; this is the shape of the fabric library.
* [Fabric durability and care](durability-and-care.md) - Makers warn about foil dulling and loss, colour bleed, pilling of printed polyester and snagging of mesh; matte tricot is the most resilient; care advice agrees on cold, alone, inside out, no softener and no heat, but conflicts on hand versus machine washing.
* [Fabric stack (outer fabric plus lining per panel)](fabric-stack.md) - A competition leotard combines two to four fabrics, and each panel is a stack of an outer fabric over an optional lining or second layer; opacity and look come from the stack, not from one material.
* [Foil, fog, metallic, glitter and novelty mesh](foil-and-glitter-mesh.md) - Sheer stretch net carrying foil dots, opal foil, a woven metallic or glitter (about 115 g/m²), plus patterned novelty meshes; used for sleeves and overlays, accent-only and barred from Spanglez at GK.
* [Glitter-coated tricot](glitter-coated-tricot.md) - Glitter applied all over 80/20 nylon spandex (about 216 g/m²) gives dense sparkle for accents and training wear, but sheds and dulls with wear and washing.
* [Hologram foil fabrics](hologram-foils.md) - Hologram fabrics (Sparkle, Opalescence, Prism, Shattered Glass, Cracked Ice, Starlet, Kaleidoscope, fish scale) carry a diffractive foil that throws angle-dependent rainbow colour; 80-83% nylon or polyester with 17-20% elastane, 200-235 g/m², classed as fragile.
* [Linings](linings.md) - Leotard linings are thin, soft stretch knits (85-92 g/m²) in a few nude tones plus white, black and brown, used as front lining, under mesh bodices and as gussets; GK's own Shadowproof composition is contradictory.
* [Matte nylon-elastane tricot](matte-tricot.md) - Matte 'lycra' (Primatex, Matt Lycra, Milliskin Matte, Vita, Malaga, Kira): 78-80% nylon / 20-22% elastane, 190-220 g/m², opaque, saturated colour; the most resilient leotard fabric.
* [Mystique (foil-dot) fabric](mystique-foil-dot.md) - Mystique is dyed tricot carrying adhesive-bonded micro-dots of metallic foil (80% nylon or polyester / 20% elastane, 200-230 g/m²); it is the dominant competition body fabric and its foil is the weak point.
* [Polyester-elastane print base](polyester-print-base.md) - White polyester-elastane tricot (SubFuse, SoftLux, Motion250, Tobago, Shiro, Funki and Pine Crest bases), 75-87% PES / 13-25% EA at 190-250 g/m², is the cloth sublimated leotards are printed on; it pills on rough surfaces.
* [Shiny tricot, satin, wet look and cire](shiny-tricot-and-wet-look.md) - Shiny nylon-elastane tricot ranges from a subtle satin glow to coated high gloss (cire, 'liquid'); 76-83% nylon / 17-24% elastane, 180-220 g/m², and it is where GK's 2026-27 new fabrics are.
* [Solid metallic foil, lamé and liquid finishes](solid-metallic-foil.md) - Continuous metallic foil or glossy coating over 80/20 nylon spandex (about 184 g/m²) gives an all-over metallic or latex-like gloss; used for accents, and its stretch is limited.
* [Stretch mesh and illusion mesh](stretch-mesh-and-illusion.md) - Fine bi-elastic stretch net (80-87% nylon / 13-20% elastane, 65-115 g/m²) is the sheer fabric for sleeves, yokes, cut-outs, nude illusion panels and crystal bases; fragile, accent-only at GK, and needs lining on the bodice.
* [Stretch properties ("four-way stretch" is not equal stretch)](stretch-properties.md) - Leotard warp knits are sold as 'four-way stretch' but mill tests show most stretch far more along the length (135-230%) than across the width (85-140%); Carvico's data sheets are the only published measurements.
* [Stretch velvet (smooth, crushed, burnout, foiled)](stretch-velvet.md) - Stretch velvet is a cut-pile knit (85% nylon / 15% elastane or 86-90% polyester / 10-14% elastane, 176-320 g/m²) whose nap makes shade depend on light and view direction; now rare as a body fabric and barred from heat-applied decoration at GK.

# Open Question

* [Fabric data nobody publishes](fabric-data-gaps.md) (draft) - No measured optical data (gloss, sparkle, foil-dot size, mesh openness, pile height), no thickness, no foil stretch figures and several maker contradictions; every fabric setting is a starting guess until physical swatches are measured.

# Process

* [Sublimation printing on polyester-elastane](sublimation-printing.md) - Sublimated leotards are printed on transfer paper and heat-transferred into white polyester-elastane at about 175-215 C; this forces a separate polyester fabric family and brings ink-palette limits on coloured bases, reorder drift, a 10% tolerance and pilling.
